skill_traces.query:
John: Hey Tim, great to see you! Any new success stories?
Tim: Hey John, I had a tough time with my English lit class. Did an analysis on this series and I think it went ok!
John: Thanks! It's a bummer about your English lit class, but you did your best. By the way, I had a career-high in assists last Friday in our big game against our rival. Yay!
Tim: Congrats! That's awesome. How did it feel being out there making those plays?
John: Thanks! It felt great being out there, making plays for my team. I love seeing my teammates succeed because of the opportunities I create for them. The atmosphere in the arena was really electric and playing against our rivals added an extra level of intensity. It was a memorable night!
Tim: Sounds incredible! Must have been quite an atmosphere. Have you had any other games that were as thrilling as this one?
John: I've had some thrilling games in my career. My favorite was when we were down 10 in the 4th and I hit the buzzer-beater shot to win. The atmosphere was incredible and it was such a thrilling experience. Those moments make me love basketball so much.
Tim: Wow, John! Moments like that make us love sports, huh? I still think about this pic you sent me a while back.
John: Yeah, that pic reminds me of when I was younger. I'd practice basketball outside for hours, dreaming of playing in big games. It was my way of dealing with doubts and stress. It's amazing how a ball and hoop can be so powerful, right?
Tim: Yeah! Sports are the best. When we're feeling down, it's a way to express ourselves and stay positive. It's awesome how much basketball has done for you. Keep going with your dreams!
John: Thanks! Appreciate the support. It's been a significant part of my life and allows me to be myself and pursue my passions. Gonna keep chasing my dreams!
Tim: Wow! It's really important to do our own thing and follow our dreams. Keep it up, you're gonna do amazing things!
John: Your encouragement means a lot. Let's keep pushing and following our dreams - we can make a difference!
Tim: Definitely. We both have so much potential! Let's keep supporting each other on our journey towards our dreams.
John: Yeah, you're super inspiring and motivating. Keep it up!
Tim: Thanks, it means a lot. Let's keep each other motivated. Bye!

selected.name: Extract Offers, Encouragement, and Advice
selected.description: Use during extraction when a message contains one person offering help, giving advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
content: During extraction, treat a single message as sufficient evidence when a speaker offers help, gives advice, encouragement, or reassurance to another person.
Create one event memory capturing the speaker, the recipient, and the gist of what was said, including any explicit guidance or offer topic.
Stop after the gist is captured; do not infer the recipient's internal feelings or expand into multiple memory kinds unless the message contains other distinct facts.
selected.rerank_reason: The session contains explicit encouragement and support from both participants, which aligns with the skill's focus on extracting offers, encouragement, and advice.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Explicit Advice and Suggestions
nearby_not_selected.description: When a message contains explicit advice, suggestions, or recommendations from one participant to another, extract them as memory candidates.
content: During extraction, treat explicit advice, suggestions, and recommendations as memory-worthy. Capture the advisor, the recipient, the advised action, and the source message.
Preserve all distinct pieces of advice and their qualifiers; do not collapse or omit details. Tentative phrasing still counts.
Represent as an event or relationship memory; create at most one candidate per distinct piece of advice.
Stop after capturing the stated advice; do not infer outcomes or expand into related topics.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Inspiration and Plan Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user mentions what inspired or motivated their current or future project.
content: During extraction, treat statements like 'X sparked ideas for my [project]' as a plan/state memory candidate.
Do not skip a turn just because it contains no direct question; extract motivation and project details from casual narrative.
Resolve relative time from the message/session timestamp and include it in the memory.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract implied vacation location memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user mentions a past vacation or trip with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), extract an event memory for that time and place, resolving relative time from the message timestamp.
content: During extraction, if a message mentions a trip or vacation with a location and a relative time (e.g., last summer, last year), create an event memory for that trip. Resolve the relative time from the message timestamp; use the country as the location if only a city is named.
Do not skip such statements just because the trip is mentioned as background (e.g., describing a photo). If the location and time are clear, extract the event.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Statements of Personal Significance
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user says an object, photo, or item reminds them of someone or something, or has personal meaning.
content: During extraction, when a user describes an object, photo, or item as reminding them of someone or something ('reminds me of', 'makes me think of', 'means ... to me'), create a candidate state memory capturing the connection.
Record who is reminded (the speaker), the object, and what it reminds them of (person, feeling, or value) in the speaker's own words.
Treat such statements as durable personal facts even though they are phrased as effects or feelings, not as direct assertions; extract at most one memory per statement.
